title: Analogical Reasoning in Science
venue: Cambridge Elements in the Philosophy of Science
core_claim: Contemporary synthesis of epistemological questions about analogy in scientific discovery/inference
ai_translation: Use as field orientation; map philosophical questions to AI transfer-control states

title: Confirmation by analogy
core_claim: Bayesian confirmation from analogy depends on background/context and a bridge hypothesis; similarities and dissimilarities bear on target support through an inferential structure
ai_translation: Do not identify similarity with confidence; model bridge hypothesis and projection relevance separately

title: The Formal Structure(s) of Analogical Inference
core_claim: Different Bayesian structures capture different kinds of analogical inference; increasing believed similarity need not always increase confirmation
ai_translation: No universal monotone similarity→transfer-confidence rule

title: Reasoning by Analogy and by Difference
venue: Journal for General Philosophy of Science 57:135-167
core_claim: Analogies are relative to domains/points of view; projection requires background meta-rules linking shared/different dimensions to projected dimensions
ai_translation: Add a projection-relevance/meta-rule layer between mapping and transfer; learn determination/separation/counter rules

title: Analogical reasoning from a context-update perspective
core_claim: Treats source target and reasoning contexts as dynamically updated belief sets; similarity emerges through AGM-style expansion contraction revision; over-analogization can arise from information loss
ai_translation: Represent source/target/reasoning context as state; allow typed belief/representation revision and audit destructive contraction

title: Tales of twin cities: what are climate analogues good for?
authors: Giovanni Valente; Hernán Bobadilla; Rawad El Skaf; Francesco Nappo
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 14:34
core_claim: Climate analogue methods face source/target non-uniqueness, averaging, non-causal correlation and inferred-property problems
ai_translation: Stress-test representation/metric choice and projection-specific validity; use sets of plausible sources

title: Extrapolating from experiments, confidently
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 13:18
core_claim: Extrapolation assumptions remain uncertain; support graphs articulate/manage interconnected uncertainty
ai_translation: Expose uncertainty over transfer assumptions/support links rather than one analogy confidence

title: Problems of Extrapolation
core_claim: Separates logical, evidential and practical problems of extrapolation; structural analogies can evidence causal comparability
ai_translation: Separate transfer logic from evidence supporting comparability and practical acceptance

title: A New Approach to Argument by Analogy: Extrapolation and Chain Graphs
core_claim: Generalizes mechanisms-based extrapolation with chain graphs and distinctive fingerprints to avoid spurious analogies/extrapolator circle
ai_translation: Localize likely mechanism breakpoints and use diagnostic target fingerprints rather than whole-source similarity

title: Extrapolation, Analogy, and Comparative Process Tracing
core_claim: Comparative process tracing refines analogical extrapolation by selectively comparing relevant mechanism stages
ai_translation: Bind projections to mechanism stages; inspect likely source-target divergence points and acquire targeted evidence

title: Extrapolating Other Consciousnesses: The Prospects and Limits of Analogical Abduction
core_claim: Analogy alone and IBE alone are inadequate; analogical abduction handles extrapolation while retaining problem-of-difference limits
ai_translation: Treat analogy as hypothesis generation embedded in explanatory competition

title: Conceptual revision: how Darwin's analogy supported his theory
core_claim: The same broad analogy changed evidential role only after substantive conceptual revisions; formal structure alone misses this
ai_translation: Allow failed analogy to trigger representation/concept revision before remapping

title: Concept and Feature Change in Scientific and Deep Neural Net Representations
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society
core_claim: Compares methodological practices for concept change in scientific representations and feature change in DNN-procured representations; argues for methodological cross-pollination
ai_translation: Treat DNN feature/relation revision as an epistemically assessable operation rather than opaque retraining

title: Model Transfer in Science
venue: The Routledge Handbook of Philosophy of Scientific Modeling
core_claim: Surveys what is transferred across scientific domains and how model transfer relates to target similarity adaptation and scientific progress
ai_translation: Type the transfer object and separate formal/model-strategy reuse from causal or outcome transfer

title: Model Transfer in the Recent History of Economics: The Case of Rational Choice Models
core_claim: Shows model forms migrate and are adapted across domains rather than simply copied; transfer can reshape target representation
ai_translation: Track model lineage adaptation and representational dependence among apparently independent source domains

title: Of Water Drops and Atomic Nuclei: Analogies and Pursuit Worthiness in Science
venue: British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 71(3):881-903
core_claim: Analogy can justify pursuit by transferring a well-understood modelling strategy without thereby confirming a target hypothesis
ai_translation: Separate GENERATE/PURSUE rewards from BELIEVE/PROJECT/ACT permissions

title: Prediction via Similarity: Biomedical Big Data and the Case of Cancer Models
authors: Fabio Boniolo; Giovanni Boniolo; Giovanni Valente
core_claim: kNN prediction depends on geometrical similarity metrics whose epistemic reliability must be assessed
ai_translation: Treat retrieval metric/feature space as part of the scientific hypothesis and benchmark it

title: Evidence and analogy in Archaeoastronomy
authors: Francesco Nappo; Giulio Magli; Giovanni Valente
core_claim: Defends context-sensitive/localist justification; field-specific norms and converging evidence govern responsible analogy; multiple imperfect analogues can jointly reconstruct targets
ai_translation: Portable control grammar plus domain-local warrant rules; multi-source partial transfer

title: Analogical reasoning: a Carnapian approach
authors: Igor Douven; Steven Verheyen; Shira Elqayam; Peter Gärdenfors; et al.
core_claim: Formalizes analogy through a Carnap-inspired similarity/conceptual-space framework
ai_translation: Compare conceptual-space similarity models with relational/causal transfer-control approaches

title: Dumb holes: universality or analogy? What makes an analogue experiment an analogue experiment?
core_claim: Analogue experiments remain analogical until externally validated as probative of the target for the purpose of inquiry; source success alone is not confirmation
ai_translation: Represent validation state and model-external/target-side evidence; allow projection-specific upgrade from plausibility to stronger license

title: What's so special about black hole simulations?
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 15
core_claim: Defends a material-analogy epistemology of terrestrial black-hole simulations and questions whether universality results alone establish an evidential function
ai_translation: Treat theoretical universality/structural equivalence as one bridge claim needing empirical/material support rather than automatic confirmation

title: The epistemic status of derivational robustness
authors: Brian McLoone; Steven Hecht Orzack; Elliott Sober
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 15:46
core_claim: Agreement among multiple model derivations does not straightforwardly have the epistemic significance of multiple independent measurements
ai_translation: Do not count confirming analogues as independent evidence without dependence/assumption analysis

title: Robustness Reexamined: Unpacking the Limits of Model-Based Robustness Analysis as Explanatory Reasoning
core_claim: Model-ensemble agreement can be epistemically weak if the ensemble inadequately samples representational uncertainty or shares hidden assumptions
ai_translation: Measure assumption/representation diversity, not superficial source diversity

title: Inferential rules for confirmatory robustness
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 16:34
core_claim: Develops derivational confirmation/disconfirmation rules; robustness can reveal dispensable auxiliaries but needs indirect empirical links to yield empirical confirmation
ai_translation: Vary/remove auxiliaries to identify invariant core; keep robustness support distinct from external target confirmation

title: Modelling Analogical Reasoning: One-Size-Fits-All?
venue: Wittgenstein and Artificial Intelligence, vol. I, ch. 9
core_claim: Explicitly frames universal-vs-local models of analogy as a problem for automating scientific reasoning with AI
ai_translation: Evaluate universal control grammar vs local warrant models; criteria for good/bad analogical inference must be computationally explicit
